discovery: Energy landscape theory and the principle of minimal frustration in protein folding
subfield: Biological physics / statistical mechanics of disordered systems
motivation: Bryngelson and Wolynes (1987) brought spin-glass statistical mechanics to the protein folding problem and formulated the principle of minimal frustration: evolved sequences have energy landscapes in which native interactions are mutually consistent, so they avoid glassy trapping. Onuchic and Wolynes then built this into the funnelled energy landscape picture. It quantitatively explains how folding can be fast and reliable despite Levinthal's paradox, predicts folding kinetics, transition-state ensembles and the role of topology, and underlies structure-based (Go-type) models that are now standard in simulation. It is a real physics achievement: a simple, falsifiable theory from the physics of random systems that changed how a large part of biology thinks. Its reach now covers misfolding, aggregation, allostery and chromosome organisation, and it helped explain why coevolution-based and AI structure prediction work. Protein structure prediction has been recognised; the underlying physical theory deserves recognition in its own right.
